title: Minimum Days to Make m Bouquets
statement:
A garden has `n` flowers in a row. Flower `i` blooms on day `bloom[i]` and stays bloomed afterwards, so on day `d` it is available if `bloom[i] ≤ d`.

To make one bouquet you need exactly `k` **adjacent** flowers (positions `i, i + 1, ..., i + k - 1`), all of which have bloomed. Each flower can be used in at most one bouquet.

Find the minimum day `d` on which you can make at least `m` bouquets. If it is impossible to ever make `m` bouquets, print `-1`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains three integers `n`, `m` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `bloom[0] ... bloom[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print the minimum day, or `-1` if `m` bouquets can never be made.

examples.explanation: On day 2 flowers 0 and 1 are open: one bouquet. On day 3 flower 3 also opens but it has no open neighbour. On day 4 flower 4 opens, giving bouquets (0,1) and (3,4), so the answer is 4.
Two bouquets of 3 flowers need 6 flowers, but there are only 4.
With k = 1 any open flower is a bouquet. Three flowers are open by day 4 (the two 1s and the 4).

hints: First rule out the impossible case: you need at least m * k flowers in total.
If you can make m bouquets on day d, you can also make them on any later day. That monotonic property suggests binary search over the day.
To check a day d, scan the row once and count how many full groups of k consecutive bloomed flowers you can form, resetting the run whenever a flower has not bloomed.
